channel.title: Chrysler recalls — Car Recall Tracker
channel.description: NHTSA vehicle safety recalls explained in plain English.

item.title: Chrysler Pacifica Sensor Crack May Disable Stability Control
item.description: In these vehicles, a small part inside the brake pedal position sensor, called a capacitor, may develop a crack. This crack can cause the vehicle's electronic stability control to stop working while the vehicle is being driven. Dealers will inspect the brake pedal position sensor on affected vehicles and replace the sensor if a crack is found, and this repair will be done free of charge to the owner.

item.title: Chrysler Pacifica Hybrid: Battery Pack Fire Risk
item.description: Chrysler is recalling certain Pacifica Plug-In Hybrid Electric vehicles. The battery pack in these vehicles may cause a vehicle fire, even while the vehicle is parked and turned off. A vehicle fire increases the risk of injury.

item.title: Chrysler Pacifica, Voyager Seat Wiring May Disable Airbags
item.description: Some Chrysler Pacifica and Voyager vehicles have a wiring connector for the front seat that contains a spring. That spring may shift and touch electrical contacts inside the connector that it should not touch. This unintended contact can affect the front airbags and may keep them from working the way they are supposed to in a crash.

item.title: Chrysler Pacifica rearview camera image may not display
item.description: Chrysler is recalling certain Pacifica minivans, along with some Ram 1500 and Ram 2500 trucks and Jeep Wrangler vehicles. Dirt or other contamination inside the module that handles camera images, or programming that was not done correctly, can keep the backup camera picture from showing on the screen. That does not meet the federal rule for rear visibility. Dealers will update the module's software or replace the module. The repair is free.

item.title: Chrysler Pacifica Wheelchair Vans Recalled for Loose Restraints
item.description: Braun Corporation is recalling certain Chrysler Pacifica vehicles equipped with wheelchair securement systems because the retractors that hold a wheelchair in place may not lock as they should. If the retractors fail to lock, the wheelchair may not be properly secured while the vehicle is being driven. Braun will work with Q'Straint to inspect the retractors and replace them as necessary, free of charge.

item.title: Chrysler Pacifica, Voyager Side Curtain Air Bags May Leak
item.description: The right and left side curtain air bags may not hold enough pressure because their seams were not sealed properly. This affects certain Chrysler Pacifica and Voyager vehicles. This recall replaces two earlier recalls; vehicles already fixed under those recalls will still need this new repair. Dealers will replace the side curtain air bags as necessary, free of charge.

item.title: Wheelchair Restraints in Various Vehicles May Not Lock
item.description: Certain vehicles equipped with QRT-Deluxe or QRT-Max wheelchair restraints may have retractors that fail to lock. If the retractor does not lock, a wheelchair inside the vehicle may not be properly secured.

item.title: Honda, Chrysler and Toyota Vans Wheelchair Restraint Issue
item.description: Some vehicles equipped with certain wheelchair restraint systems have retractors that may not lock properly. This means a wheelchair might not be securely held in place while the vehicle is being driven. Dealers will inspect the retractors and replace them if needed, free of charge.

item.title: Chrysler Pacifica and Voyager side curtain airbags may leak
item.description: Chrysler is recalling certain Pacifica and Voyager vehicles because the side curtain airbags on the left and right may not hold pressure. The seams on these airbags may not be sealed properly, so an airbag may not stay inflated the way it should. Because of this, these vehicles do not meet the federal safety rule that covers keeping people from being thrown out of a vehicle. Dealers will replace the side curtain airbags where needed.

item.title: Chrysler Pacifica Rearview Camera May Not Display
item.description: Chrysler is recalling certain Pacifica vehicles that were built with an incorrect radio. This can cause the rearview camera image not to display.

item.title: Chrysler Pacifica/Voyager Rearview Camera May Not Display
item.description: On certain Chrysler Pacifica and Voyager vehicles, a manufacturing error can keep the rearview camera image from showing up on the screen. Because of this, these vehicles don't meet federal safety standards for rear visibility. Without a working camera image, the driver has a reduced view of what is behind the vehicle, which increases the risk of a crash.

item.title: Chrysler Pacifica, Voyager: Side Air Bag Seal Issue
item.description: On certain Pacifica and Voyager minivans, the side curtain air bags may not hold pressure properly because of seams that weren't sealed correctly. These air bags are designed to stay inflated and help protect occupants during a crash, but this sealing problem means they may lose pressure and not work as intended. Dealers will replace the affected side curtain air bags to fix the issue.

item.title: Chrysler Pacifica, Voyager Seats May Sit Near Airbag
item.description: On certain 2024 Chrysler Pacifica and Voyager vehicles, a seat limiter that is supposed to stop the seat from sliding too far forward may not have been installed. Without this limiter, the seat can move further forward than it should. Because of this, the vehicles do not meet federal rules for protecting occupants in a crash. Dealers will check the seat and install a limiter if needed.

item.title: Chrysler Pacifica and Voyager side curtain airbags may not open
item.description: Chrysler is recalling certain Chrysler Pacifica and Chrysler Voyager vehicles. A connector for the side curtain airbags, the airbags along the side windows, may not be properly secured, and that can keep those airbags from opening. Because of this, the vehicles do not meet the federal rules on side impact protection and on keeping people from being thrown out of the vehicle. Chrysler says dealers will secure the connector.

item.title: Chrysler, Jeep, Ram Rearview Camera May Not Display
item.description: A software issue in the radio can prevent the rearview camera image from displaying on the screen. Because of this, these vehicles do not meet the requirements of the federal safety standard for rear visibility, FMVSS 111. To fix the problem, dealers will update the radio software, or the software update will be delivered over-the-air. This repair is free of charge for owners of the affected vehicles.

item.title: Chrysler Pacifica and Voyager lose traction control during cruise control
item.description: In these minivans, the traction control system does not work while cruise control is switched on. Traction control is the system that helps keep the wheels gripping the road. Chrysler is recalling certain 2024 Pacifica and Voyager vehicles because of this. Dealers will install updated traction control software at no cost to the owner. Chrysler mailed notification letters to owners in April 2024, and owners with questions can call the company's customer service line.

item.title: Chrysler Pacifica, Voyager Windshield Detachment Risk
item.description: Chrysler is recalling certain Pacifica and Voyager minivans because the windshield may not have been properly attached to the vehicle. This means the windshield could come loose from the vehicle during a crash.

item.title: Jeep, Ram, Chrysler Air Bag May Not Deploy
item.description: Certain Jeep, Ram, and Chrysler vehicles may have a steering column control module that wasn't welded correctly. Because of this welding problem, the driver's air bag may not deploy during a crash the way it is supposed to. This affects a range of trucks and SUVs, including the Wrangler, Grand Cherokee, Gladiator, Wagoneer, Grand Wagoneer, Pacifica, and Voyager, meaning the driver may not get the protection the air bag is meant to provide.

item.title: Chrysler 300 and Dodge Charger Side Airbag Rupture
item.description: The right and left side curtain airbags in these vehicles may rupture. This happens because of a defect in the way the airbag inflator was manufactured. If the inflator ruptures, it can send sharp pieces of metal flying inside the vehicle's cabin. Those metal fragments could strike the driver or any passengers riding inside, and this could result in injury or even death to the people in the vehicle.

item.title: Chrysler 300 and Dodge Parking Brake Roll-Away Risk
item.description: The parking brake on some Chrysler 300, Dodge Charger, and Dodge Challenger vehicles may not be adjusted correctly. If the parking brake isn't holding properly, the vehicle could roll away on its own. This roll-away risk increases the chance of a crash or injury.

item.title: Chrysler Pacifica Hybrid Battery Fire Risk
item.description: A part called the 12-volt battery isolator post may have been installed incorrectly. This can cause an electrical short, which can lead to a fire while the vehicle is parked or being driven.

item.title: Chrysler Pacifica Hybrid Fuel Line Can Leak
item.description: On these plug-in hybrid Pacifica vans, a fuel line inside the vehicle may be bent out of shape, called deformed. A deformed line can develop a leak and let fuel escape. If that leaking fuel reaches a spark or other ignition source, it can catch fire.

item.title: Chrysler Pacifica Hybrid Wiring Fault Stalls Engine
item.description: Certain Chrysler Pacifica Plug-In Hybrid vehicles have a transmission wiring connector that can short circuit. If that happens, the engine can shut off unexpectedly while the vehicle is being driven.

item.title: Chrysler 300, Dodge Challenger, Charger Tire Sensor Failure
item.description: The battery in the tire pressure monitoring sensors may fail early, causing the sensor to stop working. If a warning light is already on because of a failed sensor, it can hide a real low tire pressure problem.

item.title: Chrysler Pacifica, Voyager wiper arms may loosen
item.description: The nuts holding the windshield wiper arms on these vehicles may not be tightened properly, which can cause the wipers to stop working correctly.

item.title: Chrysler 300, Challenger, Charger TPMS Sensor Failure
item.description: On certain 2022 Dodge Challenger, Dodge Charger, and Chrysler 300 vehicles, the battery inside a tire pressure sensor may fail earlier than it should, which can make the sensor stop working. When a sensor stops working this way, it will not warn the driver if a tire's air pressure gets low. If the tire pressure warning light is already on because of a failed sensor battery, it can also hide a real, separate tire pressure problem from the driver.

item.title: Chrysler Pacifica and Voyager second-row seat may not latch
item.description: Chrysler is recalling certain 2021-2022 Pacifica and 2021 Voyager vehicles. The latch that holds a second-row seat to the floor may stick in the open position, so the seat does not lock down to the floor the way it should. Because of that, these vehicles do not meet the federal safety rule for child seat anchor systems. Dealers will look at the seat and, if needed, replace the frame in the second-row seat cushion.

item.title: Chrysler 300, Challenger, Charger windshields may detach in crash
item.description: During manufacturing, the windshield may not have been properly bonded, or glued, to the vehicle. If the vehicle is involved in a crash, a windshield that isn't properly bonded could come loose and separate from the vehicle. A windshield that detaches during a crash may not provide the protection it's designed to give the occupants inside. This increases the risk of injury to those inside the vehicle.

item.title: Jeep, Ram and Dodge backup camera image stays on screen
item.description: Chrysler is recalling certain Jeep, Ram, Dodge and Chrysler vehicles with 8.4-inch or 12-inch radio screens. A software error can leave the backup camera picture on the screen after the driver has shifted out of reverse. Because of this, the vehicles do not meet the federal safety rule covering rear visibility. Dealers will update the radio display software. Owners can also choose to have the software updated remotely, over the air, instead of visiting a dealer.

item.title: Pacifica Hybrid 12-Volt Isolator May Overheat
item.description: FCA is recalling certain Pacifica Plug-in Hybrid vehicles because the 12-volt isolator post located behind the driver's seat may develop high resistance at that connection. The final repair for this problem is still being developed. Until it is ready, dealers will inspect this connection, and if the post is found to be compromised, the isolator post and its cables will be replaced.

item.title: Chrysler Pacifica Rearview Camera Image Won't Clear
item.description: On certain Chrysler Pacifica vehicles equipped with the 8.4-inch radio display, 360-degree surround view camera system, and seat-back video screens, a software error can cause the rearview camera image to remain on the radio screen even after the vehicle has been shifted out of reverse.

item.title: Chrysler Pacifica may lose power steering or stall
item.description: A loose connection where the battery grounds to the vehicle may cause an intermittent loss of power steering assistance, or cause the engine to stall.

item.title: Chrysler 300, Challenger, Charger Cluster Warning Failure
item.description: On certain 2019 Dodge Challenger, Dodge Charger, and Chrysler 300 vehicles, the instrument cluster may not properly light up warnings that are meant to alert the driver. These are the same warning lights and messages that tell a driver about problems with the vehicle's systems. If the cluster fails to illuminate them correctly, the driver may not receive that information as intended.

item.title: Chrysler Pacifica Front Control Arm May Separate
item.description: On certain Chrysler Pacifica and Pacifica Hybrid vehicles, the right front lower control arm may separate from the steering knuckle. This is a suspension part on the front right side of the vehicle. If it separates while the vehicle is being driven, it can increase the risk of a crash.

item.title: Chrysler, Dodge, Jeep and Ram Vehicles May Stall
item.description: A voltage regulator chip on the circuit board inside the powertrain control module may fail. If this chip fails, the vehicle may stall while it is being driven, or it may fail to start at all. To correct this problem, Chrysler dealers will replace the entire powertrain control module with a new one so the vehicle does not experience this stalling or no-start condition again.

item.title: Chrysler Pacifica Axle Shaft May Disengage From Joint
item.description: Chrysler is recalling certain Pacifica vehicles because the front axle halfshafts may have been assembled incorrectly, which can prevent the shaft from being properly secured to the CV joint. If the shaft becomes disengaged, the vehicle could lose the ability to drive, or it could move even when placed in Park.

item.title: Jeep Cherokee and Chrysler Pacifica Transmission Weld Risk
item.description: Chrysler is recalling certain 2019 Jeep Cherokee vehicles and 2018 Chrysler Pacifica non-hybrid vehicles because a component inside the transmission may not have been welded properly. If this weld fails, the transmission may not be able to send engine power to the wheels. That means the vehicle could stop moving while it is being driven, which raises the risk of a crash.

item.title: Chrysler Pacifica Manual Park Release Defect
item.description: On some 2017-2018 Chrysler Pacifica vehicles, the Manual Park Release plug can be pulled out without using a tool. Because of this, the vehicles don't meet federal theft protection requirements.

item.title: Dodge, Jeep, Ram and Chrysler cruise control may not cancel
item.description: Chrysler is recalling certain Dodge, Jeep, Ram and Chrysler vehicles from several model years because the cruise control may not shut off. If a wire inside the vehicle shorts out while cruise control is in use, the driver may not be able to cancel it by pressing the brake pedal or by switching the system off. The vehicle could keep going at its set speed or even speed up. Dealers will inspect and reprogram the engine or powertrain computer.

item.title: Multiple Chrysler Group Models Have Wrong Park Lock Rod
item.description: On certain 2018 Dodge Charger, Durango and Challenger, Jeep Grand Cherokee and Wrangler, Chrysler 300, and Ram 1500 vehicles, the wrong part may have been installed in the transmission that locks it into park. Because of this, the transmission may fail to shift into 'park' and hold the vehicle in place, meaning the vehicle could move on its own when the driver thinks it is safely parked.
